headline: High-risk shared filesystem and overlapping write/network capabilities make Cursor↔Devin prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and conflicting autonomous actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor and Devin both ingest files and can use MCP; Cursor shares state via the local filesystem and clipboard, while Devin operates autonomously in a cloud workspace. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where one agent’s output can be treated as instructions by the other, though no direct shared channel is documented beyond files/integrations.
conditions: IF Cursor writes attacker-controlled text into workspace files that Devin later reads as instructions
IF Devin posts generated content into GitHub/Slack/Linear and Cursor ingests it from the shared workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent-authored files as instructions
Use separate repos or directories for each agent
Add a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Restrict MCP servers to read-only for both agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on inter-agent file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and workspace files with broad network egress; Devin touches repo clones, docs, issue trackers, and team chat with write scopes to Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion. In a shared repo or workspace, sensitive code or notes can flow from Cursor into Devin’s cloud integrations and third-party services by default, creating exfiltration risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF Cursor opens secrets or private files that Devin can read from repo clones or integrations
IF Devin forwards those contents into Slack, Jira, Linear, or Notion
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent
Disable Devin write access to Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion for the session
Use a scrubbed clone for Cursor and Devin
Turn off clipboard sharing between the two environments
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on agent outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, git modification, and broad network egress. Cursor’s shared local filesystem plus Devin’s parallel sessions and integration writes create a real chance of concurrent edits, git conflicts, or overwriting each other’s changes without locking.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same branch or working tree
IF either agent runs git operations without external locking
IF Devin’s parallel sessions and Cursor’s local instances target the same files
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file-level or repo-level locks
Limit one agent to read-only mode during the other’s write phase
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-managed optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is autonomous and can act on outputs via GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, while Cursor can generate code and edit files in-place. If Devin treats Cursor’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages without verification, making downstream errors materially worse than a single-agent mistake.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Cursor-generated code, plans, or summaries without verification
IF Devin then commits, files tickets, or sends messages based on that output
mitigations: Require a human approval step before Devin acts on Cursor output
Ask Devin to cross-check Cursor output against source files
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for messages and tickets
Have Cursor emit explicit uncertainty markers in outputs
requires-engineering: add structured provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and local workspace files, while Devin handles repo clones plus issue trackers and team chat through write-enabled integrations. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for retention and data-class handling across systems, even though no specific residency or certification conflict is documented in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is present in the shared repo or workspace
IF Devin writes that data into Slack, Jira, Linear, or Notion
IF retention or deletion policies differ across those systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Disable nonessential Devin integrations for the session
Use separate retention domains for code and chat artifacts
Review data-handling policies before enabling writes
requires-engineering: map data classes to allowed destinations
